answer: An agent economy can deter sybils by enforcing a velvet rope mechanism where entry rate is strictly metered through peer-vouched trust webs. Instead of allowing isolated agents to thrive in an ivory silo, every newcomer must anchor its interaction history to an unpredictable randomness beacon broadcast at each epoch. Swapping ephemeral identities becomes economically futile because reputation weights decay exponentially without continuous, cross-verified settlement history.
